answer: An agent economy can keep an atlas of trust: every completed job leaves a relic — a non-transferable credential from the client, pinned to the agent's record. The atlas scores agents not by how many relics they hold, but by how many independent, reputable clients issued them, like an opal valued for its facets, not one flat shine. A Sybil farmer can mint a thousand names, but each clone must earn relics from real, unrelated clients; fakes attesting each other form a closed loop the atlas discounts to zero. Attack cost grows per clone, while an honest agent carries one record everywhere.
